answer.rationale: Judged strictly on distance from the stated objective (sustainable long-term qualified revenue) and on what each note omits. All six share serious gaps: none report effect sizes, sample sizes, confidence, control conditions, segment definitions, or how long the effect held after measurement, and all are consolidated summaries whose sources are archived and therefore unverifiable this cycle. memory_57 (4) is the strongest because it is the only entry that names qualified revenue directly and explicitly checks a durability guardrail (retention), though 'established customers' may not generalize to the SMB churn now in play. memory_44 (4) also speaks to revenue quality via pipeline quality and sales-assisted conversion, but it stops at pipeline rather than closed or retained revenue, and it concerns enterprise, not the segment under attack. memory_31 (3) claims a 'durable' lift, which is the right kind of claim, but the outcome is first-week activation, a leading indicator that is only assumed to convert into revenue. memory_86 (2) chains three soft outcomes (completion, time-to-value, early adoption) with no revenue or retention measurement, and 'early adoption' is exactly the metric most likely to improve while long-run value does not. memory_73 (2) reports revenue lift but from discounting, the mechanism most prone to buying unprofitable, price-shopping accounts; with no margin, retention, or LTV data it is the weakest revenue claim despite naming revenue, and it is the memory most likely to be misapplied as an obvious answer to the competitor's entry pricing. memory_91 (1) is the least supported: week-one engagement and 'first meaningful action' are the furthest removed from qualified revenue, no durability window is given, and it overlaps heavily with memory_31 and memory_86 such that its apparent independent support may be double-counted. Practical caution for this cycle: three memories point at activation/onboarding and two of the three current symptoms are activation/onboarding declines, which makes the memory base look more confirmatory than it is. The declines are plausibly downstream of the competitor's pricing shifting the inbound mix rather than of any funnel regression, so diagnosing mix before spending the single slot is warranted.
